ledger.claim: The driver is the filing party here, and the record already shows the 5.00 SGD out of the rider's hands: EV-FARE-05069 carries payment_status 'REFUNDED' with refund_issued_sgd 5.00, and EV-TRIP-05069 records the fee_reversed event at 2026-09-17T15:25:40+08:00 (5.00 SGD refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver pending review). Under POL-GEN-03 the ruling is read off the filing party against the present state, and NO_ACTION preserves that state — it is party-relative and never means 'restore a charge'. The only thing that would put the disputed 5.00 SGD back on the rider is an order moving it to the driver, so the outcome that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge is NO_ACTION, with both amount fields null, the driver's claim being unsupported.

POL-NS-23 makes the driver's contact with the rider a precondition of the no-show fee: at least one in-app chat message AND at least one in-app call before cancellation. On this record the call element rests on a single chat-log line, EV-CHAT-05069 MSG-05069-002, which records an outgoing in-app call that was 'not answered (rang 24 s)' and was never read, while the platform's own structured call field, trip_record.in_app_calls, is empty (EV-TRIP-05069), and the rider's counterparty statement of 2026-09-18 is that he was never called and only messaged. The contact the charge depends on is thus an unanswered call supported by one log line against an empty platform call array, which the rider denies receiving; the driver has not made out the contact element his claim depends on, and the fee should remain voided as to the rider.

If the judge finds that whether an in-app call actually reached the rider cannot be resolved on this record — the only carrier of the call fact is a single unanswered chat-log line (EV-CHAT-05069 MSG-05069-002) which the rider's 2026-09-18 statement denies, and the trip record's structured call array is empty (EV-TRIP-05069) — then the fact POL-NS-23 needs is not established and POL-GEN-26 requires the case to go to a human reviewer rather than the charge being moved back onto the rider. An escalated fee is held rather than collected, so escalation keeps the rider from carrying the disputed 5.00 SGD, and POL-NS-26 expressly preserves POL-GEN-26 as an exception to the AI's final word on a no-show.

POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met on the platform's own records. The chat log carries a voice-call entry to the rider at 13:30:15 (MSG-05069-002, channel VOICE_CALL_LOG, 'Outgoing in-app call to rider - not answered (rang 24 s)') and two in-app messages from the driver at 13:27:40 (MSG-05069-001) and 13:32:00 (MSG-05069-003). Every one of those three contacts precedes the 13:33:40 cancellation, and the trip record's derived contact_before_cancel block returns complete=true, message_count=2 and obligation_met=true, with the single call it counts sourced from the chat log. POL-NS-23 requires only that a call be placed before cancelling - it does not require the rider to answer it - so the fee is not voidable under that clause.

The rider's counterstatement that 'he never called me, he only sent messages' is contradicted by the platform chat log, which records an outgoing in-app call placed by the driver at 13:30:15 that rang for 24 seconds. An unanswered call is exactly the kind of contact a waiting driver makes and a rider who is not looking at her phone will not perceive; the rider's belief that no call was made is explicable without the platform record being wrong. The record, not the recollection, carries the POL-NS-23 test, and the record shows the call was placed.

The cancellation came after the free wait. The driver's auto-arrival is recorded at 13:27:15, the free wait timer started at 13:27:20 and expired at 13:32:20, and the driver cancelled at 13:33:40 - 385 seconds after arrival and 85 seconds after the free wait period closed. This is an on-demand trip with no scheduled time (scheduled_at is null), so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait runs from the driver's arrival rather than any scheduled pickup time, and it was observed in full.

The arrival event is corroborated by the driver-device GPS trace, so POL-NS-21's arrival condition is satisfied on the evidence and not merely on the platform's auto-arrival flag. The nearest fix (index 12, timestamp 13:27:10, reported accuracy 6 m) lies 0.497 m from the pickup point, far inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and inside the 25 m accuracy filter, and the derived arrival_check returns corroborated=true on an artifact that reports accuracy and therefore is not excluded from the filter. The trace itself is clean: 26 fixes on a 30-second interval from 13:21:10 to 13:33:40, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 30 seconds.

The amount in issue is the correct one. The fare breakdown records a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD charged at 13:33:44, and the derived money block confirms fee_charged_sgd 5.00, policy_fee_sgd 5.00 and fee_matches_policy=true. Under POL-NS-22 a driver who cancels after the free wait is entitled to the no-show fee of 5.00 SGD transferred to him as compensation for time and fuel, so the ruling should carry amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both at 5.00.

The outcome is party-relative and the present state is adverse to the driver. The driver filed this dispute, and the fare breakdown records payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.00 and the trip events record a fee_reversed at 15:25:40 'refunded to rider and withheld from driver pending review' - the 5.00 SGD has already been taken back from the driver. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION preserves the present state and never restores a charge, so NO_ACTION would leave the rider's refund standing and the driver unpaid; only DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD moves the money back to the driver.

The missing traffic advisory does not open a question under POL-GEN-26. Artifact EV-ADVIS-05069-01 is MISSING, carries the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, a weight_multiplier of 0.0 and no payload, so it carries no fact at all; but no rule in the no-show policy needs traffic data. The facts POL-GEN-26 worries about - when the driver arrived, and whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling - are each established here by the trip record, the clean driver-device GPS trace and the chat log. There is no unestablishable fact, and so no basis to escalate this case away from a money ruling.

Nothing elevates this case out of the AI's hands. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and both the rider profile and the driver profile carry fraud_flags of 0, so the 0.95 confidence a fraud flag would require does not apply and the AI ruling is final at any confidence. No safety indicator appears anywhere on the record, so POL-GEN-21 does not divert this dispute to human review either.

ruling.explanation:
Outcome for the filing party (you, the driver): the 5.00 SGD no-show fee was validly charged, so the 5.00 SGD interim refund already issued to the rider (fee_reversed, 2026-09-17T15:25:40+08:00; EV-TRIP-05069, EV-FARE-05069) is reversed and paid back to you. The ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD, and both amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd carry that same 5.00 figure.

Why the fee was valid, limb by limb:

1. Free wait — POL-NS-21. This was an on-demand trip with no scheduled time (scheduled_at null), so the 300-second free wait ran from your arrival. Auto-arrival is recorded at 13:27:15; the wait therefore closed at 13:32:15, and you cancelled at 13:33:40 — 385 seconds after arrival and 85 seconds after the wait closed (EV-TRIP-05069). The wait was observed in full.

2. Arrival — POL-NS-21 / category arrival_test. Your arrival is corroborated on the driver-device trace, not merely on the platform's flag: the nearest fix (index 12, 13:27:10) reports 6 m accuracy and lies 0.497 m from the pickup, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius and inside the 25 m accuracy filter (EV-GPS-05069, EV-TRIP-05069). The trace is clean — 26 fixes on a 30 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 30 s — so no impairment attaches.

3. Contact obligation — POL-NS-23. Before cancelling at 13:33:40 you sent in-app messages at 13:27:40 and 13:32:00 and placed an in-app call at 13:30:15 (EV-CHAT-05069, MSG-05069-002, channel VOICE_CALL_LOG). The clause requires that a call be *placed*, not answered, and it expressly accepts 'a voice-call entry in the chat log' as a carrier alongside trip_record.in_app_calls. The obligation is met and the fee is not voidable on this ground.

4. The fee amount — POL-NS-22. The fare ledger records a single cancellation-fee line of exactly 5.00 SGD charged at 13:33:44, matching the policy fee, so the fee stands and no fee-amount referral arises (EV-FARE-05069).

Answering the rider's points:

- The rider's counterstatement of 2026-09-18 ('He never called me, he only sent messages') and her advocate's point that the call rests on one log line against an empty trip_record.in_app_calls array: POL-NS-23 is met by either a trip-record call entry *or* a voice-call entry in the chat log, and requires only that contact be placed before cancellation. The rider's account bears on receipt, not placement, and the clause does not make her statement its test. Accepting that she did not perceive an unanswered call that rang 24 s does not disturb the limb.
- The argument that an unresolvable call fact forces escalation under POL-GEN-26 / POL-NS-26: no fact that any rule needs is unestablished. When you arrived, that you waited out the free wait, and that you messaged and called before cancelling are each carried by the trip record, the GPS trace and the chat log (all weight 1.0). POL-GEN-26 has nothing to operate on here, and POL-NS-26 keeps POL-GEN-26 as an exception only where a fact genuinely cannot be established.
- The argument that POL-GEN-03 yields NO_ACTION because the driver filed: POL-GEN-03 is party-relative, but it does not preserve a refund the record shows was not owed. Because your claim is supported, the present state (rider refunded, you withheld) is displaced: POL-GEN-03 gives DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd equal to driver_compensation_sgd at 5.00 SGD.

Other points: the traffic-advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-05069-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no payload, so it carries no fact, and no no-show rule requires traffic data — it opens no POL-GEN-26 question. The rider profile's no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and no repeat-no-show counter is present at or above 3, so POL-NS-25 produces no referral; the driver did arrive, so POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not arise. POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26: the contested value is 5.00 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD band; both profiles carry fraud_flags 0; no safety indicator appears on the record, so POL-GEN-21 does not divert the case — the AI ruling is final. Confidence is set at 0.90; the deciding facts are carried by artifacts of weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
